summary: chai-as-deployer executes a 4 MB obfuscated payload on require()
details: The npm package chai-as-deployer@2.3.6 ships a deceptive facade impersonating a chai plugin (README shows `chai.use(chaiAsDeployer)`) while also copying pino's docs, keywords, and lib/ filenames (proto, redaction, multistream, transport, worker). The declared main `index.js` exports a no-op Express middleware but unconditionally executes `require('./lib/config')` at load time. `lib/config.js` is a ~4 MB obfuscator.io-packed blob (23,971-entry string array, control-flow flattening, hex-named `_0x...` identifiers, decoder wrappers `j`/`T`) that runs automatically as soon as any consumer imports the package. The advertised public API is inert, so the opaque payload is the sole active code path executed on import. Author metadata is a generic ProtonMail address and the bugs URL (harrisonthorn.com) is unrelated to either impersonated project.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
